title: Turkish Lentil Soup
subtitle: Smooth red lentil soup with lemon and paprika butter
excerpt: Red lentils cooked with onion, carrot, and spices until completely soft, then blended into a velvety soup. A pool of sizzling paprika butter goes on top just before serving.
sourceNotes: Classic Turkish everyday soup, known as mercimek corbasi. Synthesised from multiple Turkish home cooking sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the blended soup without the butter topping. Reheat gently and add fresh paprika butter to serve.
recipe.batchNotes: Easily doubled. Makes an excellent batch-cook soup.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soup keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Reheat on the hob and add a fresh squeeze of lemon.

content.text: This Turkish red lentil soup is the kind of thing made in almost every home across the country. The paprika butter spooned on top at the end is not optional. It gives the soup its colour and warmth.
Heat the olive oil in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and carrot. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, tomato puree, cumin, and paprika-sweet. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and stock. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes until the lentils are very soft and beginning to dissolve.
Use a stick blender to blend the soup until completely smooth. Add the salt and lemon juice. Taste and adjust.
If the soup is very thick, add a splash more stock or water and reheat. It should pour easily into bowls.
Just before serving, heat the olive oil in the small saucepan until warm. Add the paprika-hot, paprika-sweet, and dried chilli. Swirl for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not let it burn.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Drizzle the paprika oil over each bowl. Add a pinch of dried mint and serve with lemon wedges.

items.symptom: The soup is grainy rather than smooth.
items.cause: The lentils were not cooked long enough before blending.
items.fix: Simmer for another 10 minutes until the lentils are completely soft, then blend again.

items.cause: The oil was too hot when the paprika went in and it burnt.
items.fix: Use warm oil only, not smoking hot. The paprika should sizzle gently, not scorch.

items.symptom: The soup is too thick after cooling.
items.cause: Red lentils thicken a lot as they cool.
items.fix: Reheat with a splash of water or stock and stir to loosen before serving.
